query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but its poor oxygen resistance limits practical high-temperature use. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing the alloy’s useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and mechanism, the predicted change relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, the relevant temperature, atmosphere, exposure time, and mechanical-loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a 10 μm thick Al2O3 coating via plasma spray deposition on the surface of equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr in the cast state will improve its oxygen resistance at high temperatures without sacrificing its mechanical performance.
generation.intervention: applying a 10 μm thick Al2O3 coating via plasma spray deposition
generation.conditions: temperature: 1000 °C, atmosphere: air, exposure time: 100 hours, mechanical-loading boundaries: strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1
generation.mechanism: The Al2O3 coating acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion, reducing the oxidation rate of the underlying HfNbTaTiZr alloy and thereby improving its high-temperature resistance.
generation.predicted_outcome: a 30% reduction in oxidation rate and a 10% increase in yield strength at 1000 °C, relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr
generation.boundary: temperature: 1000 °C, atmosphere: air, exposure time: 100 hours, mechanical-loading boundaries: strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1
generation.uncertainty: The actual performance of the Al2O3 coating may vary depending on the deposition method, coating thickness, and surface roughness of the substrate.

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: if the oxidation rate of the coated sample is not reduced by at least 20% or the yield strength is decreased by more than 5% compared to the untreated sample, the hypothesis is falsified.
